topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture’s aims, places the hallmarks in the context of tumor progression, and frames loss of growth control as the central theme.

topics.label: Mutated signaling pathways that release growth control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how altered extracellular signaling and its downstream pathways can increase proliferation and survival or remove inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics show how cancer disrupts normal maturation, using blood-cell lineages and intestinal epithelium to illustrate the consequences.

topics.label: Cancer evasion of cellular growth-control safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect resistance to cell death and escape from replicative limits to the failure of safeguards that would otherwise restrain abnormal cells.

topics.label: Metabolic changes in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer alters metabolism, including increased glycolysis and metabolic changes that feed back on gene regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and vascular support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors use angiogenesis to obtain the oxygen and nutrients needed to grow.

topics.label: Metastatic spread, survival, and monitoring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how tumor cells disseminate, establish secondary tumors, and are detected or monitored during that process.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion: shared cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing how different routes to cancer can lead to shared hallmarks and then moves to questions and practicals.
